title: Cabinet Refinishing in Newberry, FL | Painted Kitchens
description: Cabinet refinishing in Newberry, FL for builder-grade maple, oak, and thermofoil kitchens. Bonding primer, sprayed urethane enamel, soft-close on request.
heroIntro: Love your new Newberry home but not the cabinet color the builder picked? Refinishing changes the look of the kitchen without replacing a single box.

questions: Is it cheaper to refinish or replace cabinets in a newer home?

sections.h2: Builder cabinets that are solid but the wrong color
body: In many newer homes in Arbor Greens, Newberry Oaks, and Country Way, the cabinets are fairly new, square, and structurally sound. The problem is the color or the finish. Replacing perfectly good boxes rarely makes sense, and our article on refinishing vs. replacing cabinets explains why.
Refinishing gives you a new color and a tougher surface while keeping your layout, countertops, and backsplash intact.

sections.h2: Getting paint to stick to factory finishes
body: Builder cabinets often come with slick factory lacquers or thermofoil wraps that ordinary paint will not grip. The fix is in the prep:
bullets: Thorough degreasing, since cooking residue is invisible but ruins adhesion
Scuff sanding to give the surface a tooth
Bonding primer matched to oak, maple, or thermofoil
Waterborne urethane enamel topcoats that cure hard and wipe clean

body: Restored homes near downtown sometimes have solid-wood cabinets that have been painted before, sometimes more than once. Those need failing layers sanded back and edges checked for chipping before primer. Oak with open grain can be grain-filled for a smooth, modern look or left with visible texture. Our guide to painting oak cabinets shows the difference.

Doors and drawer fronts are labelled and taken to a dust-free booth for spraying, which keeps debris out of the finish. Boxes and face frames are masked and sprayed in the kitchen. When everything has cured, doors are rehung, adjusted, and aligned. Soft-close hinges can be added on request.
While doors are away, the kitchen still works; you just have open shelves for a few days. The estimate lists the schedule so you know when doors come back.

A practical tip for new-construction owners: if your builder warranty period is still running, finish any warranty cabinet repairs such as sticking drawers or misaligned doors before we start. That way the boxes are adjusted once, and the fresh enamel is not disturbed by a service visit a week later.

Cabinets often kick off a bigger refresh. If you are repainting walls as well, we finish walls first and cabinets last. A Newberry color consultation can help you choose a cabinet color that works with flooring and counters you are keeping. See the full cabinet painting and refinishing service or our Newberry contractor page for everything else we do.

faqs.a: Yes, as long as the wrap is still bonded and not peeling. It needs scuffing and a bonding primer made for slick surfaces before enamel.
Waterborne urethane enamel cures to a hard film. Good degreasing and bonding primer are what prevent chipping, and we do not skip either.
Yes. Soft-close upgrades are available on request when the doors are reinstalled.

faqs.q: Do you refinish bathroom vanities too?
faqs.a: Yes. Vanities and built-ins get the same prep and enamel system as kitchen cabinets.
